misconceptions.description: Believing that because a page loads in the browser the HTML is complete and correct
misconceptions.trigger: learner ships HTML with no title, no real heading, or empty links because it still displays
misconceptions.feedback: Loading is not the bar. Run a publish checklist: a page needs a title, real heading tags, and working links even though broken HTML may still render.

misconceptions.description: Making text look like a heading by size alone instead of using an h1 element
misconceptions.trigger: the main title is bare text or a styled span, not an h1
misconceptions.feedback: Use an h1 for the main heading. A real heading tag is structure a screen reader and a reviewer can rely on; big text is not.

misconceptions.description: Writing an anchor with no href, or href pointing to nothing, so the link goes nowhere
misconceptions.trigger: an a element has no working href to a real file or URL
misconceptions.feedback: Every link needs a target. Point the href at the real artifact file and open the published page to confirm it works.
